 Judgment
These appeals have been filed by the injured claimant and the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 28.04.2015 passed by the M.A.C.T-XII, Ballari, in M.V.C. No.1066/2012.
M.F.A.No.101763/2015 is filed by the injured claimant seeking for enhancement of the compensation.
M.F.A. No.102724/2015 by the insurance company challenging the liability as well as the quantum of compensation awarded Tribunal

. 
2. Brief facts leading to filing of these appeals are that the injured Vinod Rathod filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by him in the road accident that took place on 10.05.2012.

It is averred that the injured appellant was traveling in a lorry bearing registration No.KA-28/9525 as a cleaner and when the said lorry reached near Halageri Seema N.H.63 the driver of the said lorry respondent No.1 Mehaboob lost the control over the lorry and dashed the lorry bearing No.KA-22/B-2964 from the hind side.

It is averred that the respondent No.1 was driving the lorry in rash and negligent manner,
caused the accident and in the said accident, the appellant has sustained grievous injuries, fractures all over the body and he has been shifted to the Koppal District Government Hospital and thereafter he was shifted to VIMS Hospital, Ballari and he was provided treatment as a inpatient from Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/
3 10.05.2012 to 23.05.2012. Later he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment and he has also taken treatment at Health City Hospital as a inpatient from 29.05.2012 to 16.06.2012 and after discharge also he has taken the follow up treatment and has spent Rs.12,00,000/- towards medical expenses and sought direction against the respondent to pay compensation to the appellant.
3. The respondent No.1 to 3 placed ex parte before the Tribunal.

The respondent No.4 entered appearance and filed statement of objections denying the claim of the appellant by contending that the respondent No.1, the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-28/9525 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and he had no valid driving licence on the date of accident and the insurer is not liable to pay compensation to the appellant.

It is further contended that one Sri Alla Bakshi was driving the lorry bearing registration No.KA-28/9525 and he was not having valid driving licence and with the collusion, the first respondent has been charge sheeted in the criminal case as driver with intention to help the appellant injured.
It is further contended that the claim of the injured is exorbitant and the same is required to be rejected.
4. The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence.
The injured appellant examined himself as PW-1 and also examined Dr.Syed Sadath Hussain as PW-2 and produced 135 documents as Exs.P-1 to P-135.
The respondents examined RW-1 to RW-4 and produced 8 documents which are marked as Exs.R-1 to R-8.

The Tribunal allowed the claim petition directing the respondent No.4 to pay the compensation with interest at 7% p.a. on the following heads:
1. For the injuries pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000-00 2.
Towards medical expenditure Rs.60,000-00 3. Towards attendant charges, extra Rs.6,600-00 nourishment and miscellaneous expenses 4.
For the loss of earnings during the Rs.5,000-00 period of hospitalization 5. for the loss of future earning capacity Rs.8,74,800-00 or for disability 6.
For the loss of future amenities of life Rs.5,000-00 TOTAL Rs.10,51,400-00 5.
Learned counsel Sri Manjunath Jadai appearing for the injured claimant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation to the injured.

It is submitted that the injured was aged about 21 years at the time of accident and was working as cleaner,
however, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured as Rs.4,500/- p.m. which is meager.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal has not added 40% of the assessed income towards the future prospects despite PW-2 doctor has opined that the appellant has sustained grievous injuries and assessed 90% as disability to the whole body.

It is also submitted that the appellant injured was hospitalised for 33 days and the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation on the heads pain and suffering, attendant charges and loss of earning during laid up period and sought for enhancement Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/
4 of compensation.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel Sri S.K. Kayakmath appearing for insurance company submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in fixing liability on the insurance company.

The complaint lodged by one Dalavar immediately after the accident reveals that Alla Bakshi was driving the lorry bearing registration No.KA-28/9525 and he has dashed against the rear portion of the stationed lorry bearing registration No.KA-22/B-2964 and the cleaner Vinod Rathod sustained grievous injuries.
The complaint further reveals that the driver Alla Bakshi was stuck between steering and cabin body of the lorry and they were taken out from the vehicle.
The said FIR is marked as Ex.P-1 and P-1(a).

The Tribunal has committed an error in disbelieving the aforesaid exhibits which have originated at an undisputed point of time, which categorically disclose that Alla Bakshi was driving the lorry,
however a false charge sheet has been filed stating that one Mr. Mehaboob was driving the lorry registration No.KA-28/9525.

It is submitted that the complaint categorically discloses that except driver and cleaner, no other persons were named in the FIR and filing of charge sheet on Mr.
Mehaboob is only with an intention grab the compensation as the driver Alla Bakshi was not having driving licence.
These facts were not properly appreciated by the Tribunal resulted in fastening liability on the insurance company and sought to interfere in the present appeal.
It is also submitted that the Tribunal has disbelieved the FIR and believed the charge sheet.
Hence, the said finding of the Tribunal is required to be interfered in the present appeal.

It is further submitted that the person who has registered the FIR, recorded the statement of the complainant, which unequivocally discloses that at the time of accident, the lorry was driven by Alla Bakshi and not by Mehaboob.
This fact has not been appreciated by the Tribunal and the charge sheet has been filed colluding with the owner of the lorry, with an intention to grab the compensation.
It is submitted that even the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side which is required to be interfered in the present appeal.
7. We have heard the learned counsel for the injured claimant and learned counsel for the insurance company and perused the appeal papers and the Tribunal records.

8. It is not in dispute that the injured Vinod Rathod has suffered grievous injuries in the road accident which took place on 10.05.2012 when the lorry bearing registration NoKA-28/9525 reached near Halageri Seema NH 64, the driver of the said lorry drove the same in rash and negligent manner and lost the control over it and dashed the stationed lorry bearing registration No.kA-22/B-6294 from hind side.

In the said accident, the appellant has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment in VIMS Hospital, Ballari, NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru and Health City Hospital and he was inpatient for 33 days and doctor PW-2 has deposed that due to the accident, the injured claimant has suffered 90% disability.
The Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,51,400/-.

Keeping these facts in mind, the following points would arise for our consideration in these appeals that:

sentences.text: 1) Whether the Tribunal is justified in fastening liability to pay the compensation on the insurance company?
2) Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.4,500/- p.m.?
3) Whether the Tribunal is justified in not awarding the compensation for future prospects ?
9. The answer to the aforementioned point No.1 is in the affirmative and point Nos.2 and 3 is in negative for the following reasons:

The injured who was traveling in lorry bearing registration No.KA-28/9525 as cleaner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident which has taken place on 10.05.2012 at about 5.00 a.m. when the driver of the lorry has drove the lorry in rash and negligent manner and hit the stationed lorry bearing No.KA- 22/B-2964 from hind side.
The learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the jurisdictional police have registered FIR which is marked as PW-1.
In the said FIR, it is reflected that the driver of the vehicle was Alla bakshi and not Mehaboob as claimed by the injured claimant and as stated in the charge sheet.
It is not in dispute that on completion of investigation, the police have filed the charge sheet against Mehaboob S/o Khaja Hussain Sab who was driving the lorry bearing No.KA-22/B-2964.

On bare perusal of the FIR, it is referred that the lorry was driven by Alla baksh however on perusal of the statement of the appellant as per Ex.P-137 wherein he has categorically stated that he and one Alla baksh have sustained injuries in the said accident and one Mahaboob was driving lorry bearing No.KA-28/9525 and immediately after the accident he has run away from the spot on seeing the injured.

The Tribunal has recorded a categorical finding that it has perused case diary (CD) dated 10.05.2012, the investigation officer has written that after the accident, he went to the spot and recorded further statement of the complainant wherein he has stated that due to darkness he could not identify the driver of the lorry and due to oversight he has named the driver of the lorry as Alla Bakshi and further stated that after the accident, one person ran away from the spot and persons who were found inside the lorry cabin was understood as driver who sustained injuries and the cleaner and by oversight he has filed complaint against the person Alla Bakshi who was holding the steering wheel of the said lorry.

It is also not in dispute that the investigation officer has registered the case against respondent No.1 and thereafter filed charge sheet on completion of investigation, against Mehaboob as driver of the lorry.

The Tribunal has satisfied itself on perusal of the case diary and charge sheet,
has come to conclusion that the naming of Alla Bakshi as driver in the FIR was a mistake and given a categorical finding based on the record that one Mehaboob was driving the lorry, we do not find any reason to disbelieve the said finding of the Tribunal.

The insurance company has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the respondent No.1/Mahaboob and not produced any evidence to substantiate their Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/
6 contention that the lorry was driven by Alla Bakshi and not by Mahaboob.

sentences.text: In the absence of any contrary evidence, there is no reason to disbelieve the charge sheet filed by the Investigation Officer.
Hence, the contention of the insurance company that the lorry bearing No.KA-28/9525 was driven by Alla bakshi and not by Mehaboob has no basis and required to be rejected.

10. The contention of the learned counsel for injured claimant that the Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured at Rs.4,500/- p.m. and it ought to have assessed as Rs.15,000/- p.m. is required to be rejected for the reason that the injured claimant has not placed any material before the Tribunal to assess the income of the injured.
In the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence to assess the income.
The Tribunal ought to have assessed the income keeping in mind the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

The accident is of the year 2012 and as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income of the injured is required to be assessed at Rs.6,500/- p.m. instead of Rs.4,500/- p.m. assessed by the Tribunal.
The contention of the injured claimant that the Tribunal has committed an error in not adding 40% of the assessed income to the total income towards future prospects is required to be considered.
The claimant injured has examined Dr. Syed Hussain as PW-2, in his testimony he has stated that the claimant has suffered various injuries which wer narrated in his affidavit.

He further deposed that the injured has lost sensation in pelvic region, loss of bowl and bladder sensation,
bedsore at the heel and genital region and ankle joint press sore and atropy of both right and leg muscles of thigh and leg, complete traumatic paraplegic present.

These observations read with disability certificate at Ex.P-112, it is evident that the injured would be unable to perform his cleaner job in the lorry which he was performing prior to road accident and would not be able to earn the income what he was earning prior to the accident in question.
Hence, he is entitled for the compensation for loss of future prospects.
In our considered view, the Tribunal has committed error in not adding 40% of the assessed income to the total income towards future prospects.
It will be useful to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and others1.

sentences.text:
Para 31 reads as under:
"31.

It is now a well-settled position of law that even in cases of permanent disablement incurred as a result of a motor accident, the claimant can seek, apart from compensation for future loss of income, amounts for future prospects as well.

We have come across many orders of different tribunals and unfortunately affirmed by different High Courts, taking the view that the claimant is not entitled to compensation for future prospects in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement.
That is not a correct position of law.
There is no justification to exclude the possibility of compensation for future prospects in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement.

Such a narrow reading (2023) 3 SCC 439 is illogical because it denies altogether the possibility of the living victim progressing further in life in accident cases-and admits such possibility of future prospects, in case of the victim's death."
11.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of earning during the period of hospitalisation.

In our considered view, the injured claimant was hospitalised for a period of 33 days Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/

The contention of the injured claimant that he has suffered grievous injuries and is a bachelor and has lost the marriage prospects due to the injuries sustained by him.

On meticulous scrutiny of evidence of PW-2 Dr. Syed Hussain, who has entered the witness box and deposed that the injured claimant has taken treatment in 3 hospitals and he was inpatient and suffered the following fractures :
a) Fracture right illac bone pressed.
b) Fracture right medial mellous of tibia pressed.
c) Fracture left medial mellous of tibia pressed.
d)Fracture D12 vertibra compression fracture with traumatic paraplegia present.
He has further deposed that "I found that loss of sensation till pelvic region, loss of bowl and bladder sensation, bed sore at heel and gelatal region and ankle joint pressure sore.
Atropy of both right and left mussels of thigh and leg, complete traumatic paraplegia present."

It is true that PW-2 is not the treated doctor, however the disability certificate at Ex.P-112, photographs at Exs.P-113 to P-118 and the evidence of PW-1 establishes the fact that the injured claimant has sustained serious injuries and suffered disability at 90%.
Keeping these evidence in mind, we are of the view that the injured claimant has lost the marriage prospects.

Hence, the claimant is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/-
as compensation under the head loss of marriage prospects.

As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Erudhaya Priya referred supra.
12.

Rs.6,500+40% = 9,100 x 12 x 18 x 90/100 = 17,69,040/-

ORDER
(i) M.F.A.No.101763/2015 filed by the injured claimant is allowed in part.
(ii) M.F.A.No.102724/2015 filed by the insurance company is dismissed.

(iii) The impugned judgment and award dated 28.04.2015 passed by the M.A.C.T-XII, Ballari, in M.V.C. No.1066/2012, is modified and the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.11,09,240/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
(iv) The respondent No.4 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.

(v) In case of deposit, 50% of the enhanced amount shall be kept in the fixed deposit in the name of appellant/claimant for a period of 3 years and he is entitled to withdraw periodical interest accrued on the deposit.
Remaining amount shall be released in favour of the appellant/ claimant.

opennyai_summary.facts:
M.F.A. No.102724/2015 by the insurance company challenging the liability as well as the quantum of compensation awarded Tribunal
. 
2. Brief facts leading to filing of these appeals are that the injured Vinod Rathod filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by him in the road accident that took place on 10.05.2012.
It is averred that the respondent No.1 was driving the lorry in rash and negligent manner,
caused the accident and in the said accident, the appellant has sustained grievous injuries, fractures all over the body and he has been shifted to the Koppal District Government Hospital and thereafter he was shifted to VIMS Hospital, Ballari and he was provided treatment as a inpatient from Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/
3 10.05.2012 to 23.05.2012. Later he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment and he has also taken treatment at Health City Hospital as a inpatient from 29.05.2012 to 16.06.2012 and after discharge also he has taken the follow up treatment and has spent Rs.12,00,000/- towards medical expenses and sought direction against the respondent to pay compensation to the appellant.
The Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,51,400/-.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel relying on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Erudhaya Priya Vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., in Civil Appeal Nos.2811- 2812/2020 submits that the appellant is entitled for the compensation for loss of matrimonial prospects as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above decision.
10. The contention of the learned counsel for injured claimant that the Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured at Rs.4,500/- p.m. and it ought to have assessed as Rs.15,000/- p.m. is required to be rejected for the reason that the injured claimant has not placed any material before the Tribunal to assess the income of the injured.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. It is not in dispute that the injured Vinod Rathod has suffered grievous injuries in the road accident which took place on 10.05.2012 when the lorry bearing registration NoKA-28/9525 reached near Halageri Seema NH 64, the driver of the said lorry drove the same in rash and negligent manner and lost the control over it and dashed the stationed lorry bearing registration No.kA-22/B-6294 from hind side.
Keeping these facts in mind, the following points would arise for our consideration in these appeals that:
Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/
5
1) Whether the Tribunal is justified in fastening liability to pay the compensation on the insurance company?
2) Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.4,500/- p.m.?
3) Whether the Tribunal is justified in not awarding the compensation for future prospects ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Tribunal has recorded a categorical finding that it has perused case diary (CD) dated 10.05.2012, the investigation officer has written that after the accident, he went to the spot and recorded further statement of the complainant wherein he has stated that due to darkness he could not identify the driver of the lorry and due to oversight he has named the driver of the lorry as Alla Bakshi and further stated that after the accident, one person ran away from the spot and persons who were found inside the lorry cabin was understood as driver who sustained injuries and the cleaner and by oversight he has filed complaint against the person Alla Bakshi who was holding the steering wheel of the said lorry.
It is also not in dispute that the investigation officer has registered the case against respondent No.1 and thereafter filed charge sheet on completion of investigation, against Mehaboob as driver of the lorry.
The Tribunal has satisfied itself on perusal of the case diary and charge sheet,
has come to conclusion that the naming of Alla Bakshi as driver in the FIR was a mistake and given a categorical finding based on the record that one Mehaboob was driving the lorry, we do not find any reason to disbelieve the said finding of the Tribunal.
The insurance company has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the respondent No.1/Mahaboob and not produced any evidence to substantiate their Vinod @ Vinod Rathod vs Mehaboob S/O Khaja Hussain Sab on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13912189/
6 contention that the lorry was driven by Alla Bakshi and not by Mahaboob.
In the absence of any contrary evidence, there is no reason to disbelieve the charge sheet filed by the Investigation Officer.
In the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence to assess the income.
The Tribunal ought to have assessed the income keeping in mind the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year 2012 and as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income of the injured is required to be assessed at Rs.6,500/- p.m. instead of Rs.4,500/- p.m. assessed by the Tribunal.
Hence, he is entitled for the compensation for loss of future prospects.
In our considered view, the Tribunal has committed error in not adding 40% of the assessed income to the total income towards future prospects.
It will be useful to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and others1.
, the injured claimant is entitled for another Rs.15,000/- for loss of income during laid up period.
Keeping these evidence in mind, we are of the view that the injured claimant has lost the marriage prospects.

16. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER
(i) M.F.A.No.101763/2015 filed by the injured claimant is allowed in part.
(ii) M.F.A.No.102724/2015 filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
(iii) The impugned judgment and award dated 28.04.2015 passed by the M.A.C.T-XII, Ballari, in M.V.C. No.1066/2012, is modified and the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.11,09,240/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
(iv) The respondent No.4 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(v) In case of deposit, 50% of the enhanced amount shall be kept in the fixed deposit in the name of appellant/claimant for a period of 3 years and he is entitled to withdraw periodical interest accrued on the deposit.
Remaining amount shall be released in favour of the appellant/ claimant.
(vi) Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
(vii) Draw modified award accordingly.
